svg.title: Figure 3 · One turn of the loop
svg.desc: Four lanes: User, Model, Harness, Execution environment, as a sequence (not the nesting of Figure 1). Numbered steps: 0 the request comes in through a user interface (chat tool, code tool, API or other); 1 harness sends the context; 2 model proposes text, tool calls, or both; 3 harness checks the approval policy or permission mode, and rules, a reviewer model or a person approve or block; 4 the tool runs; 5 harness writes the result to the transcript and compacts as the context nears its limit; loop until a response has no tool calls or a limit is hit. Exit: no tool calls ends the loop; the harness returns the text. One run = the loop from start to stop. Anthropic documents the loop this way; OpenAI's held documents agree where they speak; part of OpenAI's side rests on an unverified lead. Added in v0.2: lettered limit markers matching Figure 1 and a strip showing the context growing turn by turn up to the context window and shrinking after compaction. Added in v0.7: the User lane and step 0.
svg.text: Figure 3 · One turn of the loop: the model proposes, the harness decides what runs

calls, or a limit is hit:

g.text: no tool calls: the loop ends
The model proposes; the harness executes, permits and caps. Anthropic documents the loop this way; OpenAI's held documents agree where they speak (October 2026).
The loop, repeated from start to stop, is one run; in a product, a session. The lanes show a sequence, not the nesting of Figure 1.
The context, turn by turn: step 1 sends all of it, every call (Codex; Anthropic's Messages API)
Each turn adds the model's proposal and the
tool's result to the pile. The whole pile is sent
on the next call (Codex; Anthropic's Messages
API). Near the context window (A) the harness
or the vendor's API compacts (C): it summarises
older turns so the run can continue.
